subject: PrivDep: Data exposure acceptance criteria & CMK custody checkpoints
messages:
From: Karen Lee <legal@medisys.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medisys.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: PrivDep: Data exposure acceptance criteria & CMK custody checkpoints

Marcus —

Thanks for the DPA draft. Before we take this to procurement I need clarity on three specific items for our security and legal teams:

1) Custodian and key custody: Medisys will insist on customer-managed CMKs (BYOK) for the private deployment. We need explicit language that the Redwood operator does not have access to plaintext customer data or the CMK material. Please explain how KMS integration will prevent operator access and what evidence you can provide.

2) Data exposure acceptance windows: If an operator break-glass is required for forensic purposes, we need an acceptance checklist (who authorizes, which logs are captured, retention windows, and escalation path).

3) Subprocessors & cross-border transfers: Provide the current list of subprocessors that will touch telemetry or logs, and confirm any cross-border gating for EU/UK data.

Attached is our template that highlights these areas; please send a proposed redline or a short matrix that maps your commitments to our asks.

We'd like to lock answers by EOD Friday so procurement can push the SOW.

—Karen Lee
General Counsel, Medisys Inc
Attachments: DPA_Redwood_Medisys_questions_20250610.docx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karen Lee <legal@medisys.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDep: Data exposure acceptance criteria & CMK custody checkpoints

Karen —

Thanks for the clear ask. High level answers below and a proposed artifact set attached: a one-page custody checklist and a short DPA redline. Happy to walk through.

1) Customer-managed CMKs (BYOK) — Commitment: Customers provide the CMK and control the KMS project/tenant. Redwood integrates via a strict KMS API (no key material leaves the customer KMS). Operators have no ability to export keys or decrypt ciphertext. Evidence we can provide: architecture diagram, integration runbook, and a demo of a limited-key operation (no plaintext revealed).

2) Break-glass / forensic windows — Proposal:
  • Authorization: Dual-approver from customer CS + legal (via the documented action list).
  • Scope: Operator actions allowed only to mount diagnostic artifacts; never to exfiltrate model inputs/outputs.
  • Logs: All operator sessions are session-recorded (Timestamps, commands, and any data references) and retained for 2 years by default (adjustable).
  • Escalation: Immediate notification to the customer security contact, preserved immutable evidence bundle.

3) Subprocessors & transfers — Current plan: telemetry and build orchestration are handled by Redwood subteams inside the US; we will provide a named subprocessor list and commit to a cross-border gating workflow (e.g., explicit customer consent + SCCs/appropriate basis before transfer).

Next steps I propose: attach a one-page "Custody & Exposure Checklist" and a DPA redline. Would you prefer a 30-minute call Thursday or a written redline by EOD Thursday?

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | marcus.lin@redwood.com
Attachments: DPA_Redwood_Medisys_draft_20250610.pdf; privdep-key-boundaries-slide.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDep: Data exposure acceptance criteria & CMK custody checkpoints

Looping in technical clarifications for the redline. Quoting Marcus below for context:

> 1) Customer-managed CMKs (BYOK) — Commitment: Customers provide the CMK and control the KMS project/tenant. Redwood integrates via a strict KMS API (no key material leaves the customer KMS).

Proposed clarifications to include in the DPA redline (short bullets we should offer Karen):
  - Clarify that Redwood never receives plaintext in worker memory tied to customer content; runtime uses envelope encryption and a customer CMK only to unwrap ephemeral session keys inside a secure enclave boundary.
  - Operator interfaces expose only masked telemetry and aggregated counters. Any session-level diagnostic capture is redacted by default; redaction rules are part of the runbook.
  - Attestation cadence: provide quarterly technical attestations plus on-demand audit access under NDA for the customer SOC team.
  - Subprocessor list: include names and roles, and add a 30-day notice period for new subprocessors touching telemetry/logs.

Open question for sales/legal: do we accept a 48-hour emergency operator window for break-glass if dual-approval is captured? My preference: insist on written approval from the customer's security PO and generate immutable evidence (signed ticket + session recording).

I can draft the precise contract language for the KMS paragraph and the break-glass clause — will attach to the redline.

—Irene
Director, Applied Security, Redwood Inference
Attachments: data-exposure-checklist.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karen Lee <legal@medisys.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@medisys.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDep: Data exposure acceptance criteria & CMK custody checkpoints

Karen —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a consolidated redline that incorporates the technical clarifications Irene suggested and a one-page custody checklist. Summary & proposed MAP:

Summary of commitments:
  • BYOK: Customer-managed CMKs; Redwood cannot export key material or decrypt outside approved runtime flows.
  • Break-glass: Dual-approval (customer security + legal) required; operator sessions recorded; immutable evidence bundle created and shared. 48-hour emergency window allowed only with explicit written sign-off.
  • Subprocessors: Named list attached; 30-day notice for additions that touch telemetry/logs.
  • Attestations: Quarterly technical attestations; on-demand audit access under NDA.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
  1) EOD Thu, Jun 12 — Medisys confirms whether redline language is acceptable or flags areas for call.
  2) Mon, Jun 16 — If accepted, schedule a 30-minute technical call to demo KMS integration (Irene + Karthik to host).
  3) Wed, Jun 18 — Proc loop and sign SOW (if procurement approves).

Please confirm whether Thursday call or written redline works for you. If written is easiest, we will push the DocuSign link and prepare a HubSpot update (Deal D-9142-MED).

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
